items.hook: The best books to read in October: new paperbacks from Zadie Smith, Thomas Pynchon and Francis Spufford
items.body:
Looking for a new reading recommendation? Here are some brilliant new paperbacks, from a time-travelling fantasy novel to an eclectic essay collection. Discuss what you’re reading in paperback in the comments

***

items.hook: Negus Mikael, marching on the Ethiopian capital in support of his son Emperor Iyasu V, is defeated by Fitawrari Habte Giyorgis, securing the throne for Empress Zewditu I.
items.body: The Battle of Segale was a civil conflict in the Ethiopian Empire between the supporters of Empress regent Zewditu and Lij Iyasu on 27 October 1916, and resulted in victory for Zewditu. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Su'e pian, also Su E Pian, translated into English as The Moon Goddess or The Lady of the Moon, is a Chinese erotic novel by an anonymous writer published in the late Ming dynasty.
items.body: It follows the sexual escapades of Wu Sansi (武三思) and his concubine, Su'e (素娥). Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: The 1997 Asian financial crisis causes a crash in the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
items.body: A financial crisis gripped much of East and Southeast Asia during the late 1990s. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: ‘Godzilla Minus One’ director Takashi Yamazaki to make English-language debut on ‘Grandgear’
items.body: Sam Nivola and Nico Parker to star, Paul Giamatti understood to be in talks.

items.hook: Constantine the Great is said to have received his famous Vision of the Cross.
items.body: Constantine I, also known as Constantine the Great, was Roman emperor from AD 306 to 337 and the first Roman emperor to convert to Christianity. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Frankenstein's Aunt Returns is a novel by Allan Rune Pettersson that was first published in Sweden in 1989.
items.body: The book is a sequel to the 1978 book Frankenstein's Aunt. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: War and Remembrance is a novel by Herman Wouk, published in October 1978 as the sequel to Wouk's The Winds of War (1971).
items.body: The Winds of War covers the period 1939 to 1941, and War and Remembrance continues the story of the extended Henry and Jastrow families from 15 December 1941 through 6 August 1945. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: J. S. Bach leads the first performance of Ich will den Kreuzstab gerne tragen, BWV 56, one of few works he called a cantata.
items.body: Johann Sebastian Bach was a German composer and musician of the late Baroque period. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: The 100 best novels of all time
items.body: The top 100 novels of all time published in English, as voted for by authors, critics and academics worldwide. How many have you read?

items.hook: Leicester City F.C. owner Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha dies in a helicopter crash along with four others after a Premier League match against West Ham United at the King Power Stadium in Leicester, England.
items.body: Leicester City Football Club is a professional football club based in Leicester, East Midlands, England. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Jay-Z to perform at Super Bowl half-time show
items.body: The rapper has been involved with the show for years but has never before performed at the NFL championship game.

items.hook: Meghan to co-host Junior MasterChef Australia
items.body: The Duchess of Sussex says she "can't wait" to take part in the programme, which will air next year.

items.hook: Night on the Galactic Railroad , sometimes translated as Milky Way Railroad, Night Train to the Stars or Fantasy Railroad in the Stars, is a Japanese fantasy novel by Kenji Miyazawa written around 1927.
items.body: The nine-chapter novel was posthumously published by Bunpodō (文圃堂) in 1934 as part of Complete Works of Kenji Miyazawa Vol. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Major Rudolf Anderson of the United States Air Force becomes the only direct human casualty of the Cuban Missile Crisis when his U-2 reconnaissance airplane is shot down over Cuba by a Soviet-supplied surface-to-air missile.
items.body: Rudolf Anderson Jr. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Goodbye is a 1918 British drama film directed by Maurice Elvey and starring Margaret Bannerman, Jessie Winter and Donald Calthrop.
items.body: It was based on a novel by John Strange Winter. The world is stranger than it lets on.
